title: Golden Zone Method: Structural Capacity and Existence of Prime Numbers in Legendre Intervals
content: The paper provides a detailed study of the structure of the distribution of prime numbers in sublinear intervals of the form Ik = (pk, pk + 2√pk + 1) and Legendre intervals Ln = (n2, (n + 1)2). The research and analysis of the problem are conducted through the prism of a deterministic approach based on the Rigid Sieve algorithm. Unlike classical probabilistic models, this study is based on the internal arithmetic structure of sublinear zones and the dynamics of their sterility within primorial filters. This study examines the mechanism for generating vacancies for prime numbers, which arises due to the outpacing growth of interval length compared to the filtering power of new divisors. Analysis of the self-regulating structure of intervals allows us to establish the stability of the chain of prime numbers along the entire number line, providing new grounds for verifying Legendre’s hypothesis. The presented theoretical calculations are confirmed by the results of large-scale numerical simulations conducted in the range up to 1012.
